creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Signals and Systems
Linear Systems
Time-Invariant Systems
Causality
BIBO Stability
dublinCore.description: Run linearity, time-invariance, causality and BIBO stability tests on eight example continuous-time systems. Each test overlays the two signals that the property says must be equal, reports whether they match, and explains the true classification of the system.

topic: System properties: linearity, time-invariance, causality, stability and memory
learningObjectives: Explain the superposition principle and test a system for linearity
Distinguish time-invariant systems from time-varying systems using a shifted input
Determine whether a system is causal by comparing outputs for inputs that agree up to a given time
Classify a system as BIBO stable or unstable from its response to a bounded input
Evaluate why a single matching example cannot prove that a system has a property

misconceptions.misconception: A system whose equation contains t multiplied by x(t) is nonlinear
misconceptions.correction: y(t) = t x(t) obeys superposition, so it is linear; the gain t depends on time, which makes it time-varying
misconceptions.evidence: Select the time-varying multiplier: the linearity curves coincide, but the time-invariance curves separate by t0 times the input amplitude

misconceptions.misconception: Adding a constant to the signal keeps a system linear
misconceptions.correction: The offset system y(t) = x(t) + 1 maps a zero input to a nonzero output, which violates superposition
misconceptions.evidence: Select the offset system and the linearity test: the maximum difference equals the amplitude A for every setting

misconceptions.misconception: One matching example proves that a property holds
misconceptions.correction: A property must hold for every input; one counterexample disproves it, but matching curves only show it for those inputs
misconceptions.evidence: Select the squarer, linearity test, A = 1 and t0 = 4 s: the curves coincide although the squarer is nonlinear

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Input and output plots for eight example systems. A System menu and a Test menu choose the system and the property test, and sliders set the amplitude, frequency and time shift of the test input. Five badges list the true properties of the selected system, and a panel reports whether the two compared signals match.

responsiveBreakpoints.description: Below 600 px the property badges switch to two lines, the System menu takes the whole first row, and the Test menu moves beside the time-shift slider

controls.label: System
controls.description: Chooses one of eight example systems: amplifier, linear filter, time-varying multiplier, squarer, compressor, predictor, integrator or offset

options.label: Linear filter: y(t) = integral of x over the last 1 s
Integrator: y(t) = integral of x from -infinity to t

controls.label: Test
controls.description: Chooses the property test: linearity, time-invariance, causality or BIBO stability

controls.label: Amplitude A
controls.description: Sets the amplitude A of the test input (the weight of x1 in the linearity test, the burst amplitude, or the bound of the step)

controls.label: Frequency f
controls.description: Sets the frequency of the sine burst used as the test input; greyed out for the stability test, which uses a step

controls.label: Time shift t0
controls.description: Sets the time shift t0: the delay in the time-invariance test, the start of the pulse in the linearity test, the time where the two inputs first differ in the causality test, and the start of the step in the stability test

visualElements.description: Five badges give the true classification of the selected system: linear, time-invariant, causal, BIBO stable and memoryless; the badge for the running test has a heavy outline
Input plot: the test input signals, including the bound +/-A (dotted) for the stability test
Output plot: the two output signals that the property says must be equal, as a solid blue and a dashed orange curve, with a red trace for any output difference before t0 in the causality test
Verdict panel with the maximum difference and a one-line reason why the property holds or fails

model.description: Continuous-time systems are simulated on a 0.01 s grid from -8 s to 14 s and plotted from -2 s to 10 s; each test builds the two signals that a property says must be equal and reports their maximum difference
equations: Linearity: T[a x1 + b x2] = a T[x1] + b T[x2]
Causality: y(t0) depends only on x(t) for t <= t0
algorithms: Sample-by-sample system evaluation on a fixed grid
Running sum for the integrator and the 1 s linear filter
assumptions: Property badges show the analytically known classification; the plotted comparison is one numerical example
limitations: One example can disprove a property but cannot prove it
Stability is tested only with a bounded step

instructionalStrategies: Compare systems by changing one test at a time
extensions: Add a system that is not memoryless and not invertible
